description_en: Vana Bāhāḥ is a branch of Bu Bāhā. It is situated to the east of Bu Bāhāḥ, on the left-hand side of the street leading to Mahāpāl. The Bāhāḥ can be accessed through a narrow alley and a decorative arched gate at the south-east corner of its courtyard . The three-storey main monastic building faces east and is furnished with a brass-clad door which has atoraṇaat its centre and two small lattice windows on either side. The floor level has been separated by layers of timber cornice - this, too, is covered in brass sheets. The whole façade of the building is clad in ceramic tiles with floral patterns. The first floor has a ribbon windowpasukājhyāwith five openings flanked with two small aedicules. On the second floor, one can find a central three-bay window (sopā jhyā) with latticework. The second floor has four struts at its base and two on the sides, with figures of deities holding up the overhanging tiled gable roof. At the centre of the ridge is a finial of a brass-clad stone stupa. The adjoiningguthibuilding to the north is being reconstructed and has even encroached upon the roof structure on the western side.The main building, adharmadhātu, a central two-storieddegacā, apañcāvalīyuktacaityaand abāhācāare lined up along the east-west axis fo the courtyard. The southern end wall of thebāhāḥcacollapsed as a result of the 2015 earthquake. Twocaitya, aśikharakūṭa caityato the south and aśikharokūṭotpanna jinālaya caityato the north are aligned with the central temple structure along the north-south axis. At theīśāna koṇa(north-east) corner of the courtyard is a well; this has been positioned according to thevāstu. There is a smallvajradhātu caityain a small courtyard behind theguthibuilding.At the top of the roof on the ridge there is a stonestūpawith four Buddhas on four directions. The upper drum and theharmikaare clad in brass sheets, and possibly also gold plated.The sanctum is located on the ground floor of the three-tired temple. An east-facing image of Akṣobhya Buddha is enshrined within it. Above the entrance of the sanctum one can find a toraṇa: this is clad in bronze and contains an image of a standing Mahāvairocana flanked by Mahākṣobhya on his right and Mahā Amitābha on his left. Above him, one can find images of Mahāratnasaṃbhava and Mahāmoghasiddhi. Above thetoraṇais an image of Vajrasattva. Two niches can be found on either side of the entrance: these symbolise Hanumāna. To the right-hand side of the entrance is a stone image of Halāhala Lokeśvara in asthānakagesture and to the left is a stone image of Tārā. She is holding a lotus stalk in her left arm and indicating avaradagesture with her right arm. These images of Lokeśvara and Tārā were installed in NS 916. A bell dated NS 1034 hangs to the right of the entrance.On the first floor of the main shrine, a window with five openings (pāsukhā jhyāḥ)symbolizes Five Buddhas. This window is flanked by two smaller windows. On the top floor of the shrine, one can find a triple window symbolizing the three gems of Buddhism (Buddha,dharmaandsaṅgha). The roof of the shrine is tiled and one can see acaitya-shaped pinnacle on top of it. Six struts with encarved images of various deities support the roof. Modern tiles cover the entire frontal facade of the god house and iron fences are fixed in front of the main entrance for its protection.A temple with acaityainside sits at the centre of the courtyard, and is accompanied by adharmadhātu maṇḍala, aśikharakūṭotpanna jinālaya caitya, one well, onepañcāvaliyukta caitya, and oneśikharakūṭa caitya. Another temple lies to the south of the Bāhāḥ. Its sanctum contains a stone image of Akṣobhya and a woodentoraṇawith an image of Mahāvairocana hangs above its entrance. The 2015 earthquake damaged the southern part of the temple and even the frontal facade is now supported by wood.It is believed that Ujotadeva established this Vihāra. Under his name, this Vihāra is also called Ujotadeva Vihāra. One of the inscriptions informs the reader that he enshrined the image of the main deity in NS 715. However, a palmleaf manuscript dated NS 700 mentions Ujotadeva and Vana Vāhā, which indicates that in NS 715 he may have renovated the Vihāra rather than constructing it.
description_ne: यो यशोधर महाविहार, बु बाहा:को शाखा विहार हो । बु बाहा:को पूर्वतिर अवस्थित यस विहारको क्वा:पा:देग: अर्थात् मुख्य मन्दिर तीनतले छ । भुइँतलामा पूर्वाभिमुख अक्षोभ्य बुद्धलाई क्वापाद्य:को रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ । क्वा:पा:द्य:को गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने द्वारको माथि पित्तलले मोडेको कलात्मक तोरण राखिएको छ । तोरणको बीचमा उभिएका महावैरोचन अंकित छ । महावैरोचनको दायाँ महाअक्षोभ्य, बायाँ महाअमिताभ बुद्ध छन् भने माथि महारत्नसम्भव र महाअमोघसिद्धिको प्रतिमा छ । तोरणको माथि वज्रसत्त्वको प्रतिमा छ । मूलद्वारको दायाँ-बायाँ हनुमान्को प्रतीकस्वरूप गवाक्ष बनाइएका छन् । प्रवेशद्वारको दायाँ स्थानक मुद्राको प्रस्तरको हलाहल लोकेश्वर राखिएको छ भने बायाँतिर प्रस्तरकै ताराको मूर्ति छ । ताराको दायाँ हात वरद मुद्रामा छ भने बायाँ हातले कमलको डाँठ समातेको देखिन्छ । ती दुबै मूर्ति नेसं ९१६ मा स्थापना गरिएका थिए । प्रवेशद्वारको दायाँ नेसं १०३४ मा स्थापना गरिएको घण्टा राखिएको छ ।क्वा:पा:छेँको पहिलो तल्लामा पञ्चबुद्धको प्रतीक स्वरूप पित्तलको पासुखाझ्या: राखिएको छ । उक्त झ्यालको दायाँ र बायाँ एक-एकवटा सानो झ्याल राखिएको छ । सबभन्दा माथिल्लो तल्लामा त्रिरत्नको प्रतीक स्वरूप त्रिखाझ्याल (triple window) ठूलो झ्याल राखिएको छ । क्वा:पा:छेँमा झिंगटीको छाना राखिएको छ । छाना अड्याउन विभिन्न देवता अंकित ६ वटा कलात्मक टुँडाल राखिएका छन् । छानाको सबैभन्दा माथि चैत्यलाई गजूरको रूपमा राखिएको छ । सम्पूर्ण क्वा:पा:छेँलाई टायल राखी सिंगारिएको छ । क्वा:पा:छेँको अगाडि फलामको बार राखी सुरक्षित गरिएको छ ।विहारको मध्यभागमा चैत्य रहेको सानो मन्दिर बनाइएको छ । विहार परिसरमा धर्मधातु मण्डल, शिखरकूटोत्पन्न जिनालय चैत्य, इनार, पञ्चावलियुक्त चैत्य र शिखरकूट चैत्य रहेका छन् । विहारको दक्षिणी भागमा अर्को सानो क्वा:पा:छेँ रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रस्तरको अक्षोभ्य रहेको उक्त क्वा:पा:छेँको प्रवेशद्वारमा महावैरोचन अंकित काष्ठ तोरण राखिएको छ । सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले यस द्य:छेँको दक्षिणतिरको भाग भत्किएको छ भने अगाडिको भागमा पनि टेको लगाइएको छ ।यो विहार उजोतदेवले निर्माण गरेको मानिन्छ । उनकै नामबाट यस विहारलाई उजोतदेव विहार पनि भनिन्छ । अभिलेखअनुसार नेसं ७१५ मा उजोतदेवले क्वा:पा:द्य: स्थापना गरेका थिए । तर नेसं ७०० को ताडपत्रमा नै उजोतदेव र वनबहाको उल्लेख आइसकेको देखिन्छ । त्यसैले उजोतदेवले नेसं ७१५ मा विहार स्थापना गरेको नभई जीर्णोद्धार मात्र गरेको बुझिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of kvāpādyḥ at Vana Bāhāḥ

historical_events.event_description: A palmleaf deed recording a gift of house and land from Jaya Purandara Siṃha, a king of Lalitpur, to Vajrācārya Ujotadeva, a resident of Bu Bahāla mentions Ujotadeva and Vana Bāhāḥ.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of golden Śākyamuni at Vana Bāhāḥcā
historical_events.event_description: A goldenśākyamuniwas installed at Vana Bāhācā. The donors were Jittapālaju, his wife Hṛdaya and his son. They lived to the south-east of the Bubāhāla.
Donation oftoraṇatokvāḥpāḥdyaḥof Vana Bāhācā by a group ofguṭhīmembers.
This Caitya was established during the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla by Lakṣmī Candra in memory of their late son Ratna Jyoti. They also donated land to fund its worship and annual rituals.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of a stone statue of Buddha
historical_events.event_description: Vipraśī, his two wives Pūrṇeśvari and Ratna Lakṣmī, and his son Rakṣa Narasiṃha established a new stone Buddha image (Kvāpādyo) at Wana Bāhācā because the previous one was stolen.

historical_events.event_name: Consecration of Halāhala Lokeśvara and Tārā on either side of the entrance to Kvāpādyo
historical_events.event_description: Pūrṇa Siṃhadeva, his wife Ranhamati and other family members consecrated Halāhala Lokeśvara and Tārā on either side of the entrance to Kvāpādyo in memory of grandfather Bharaju, grandmother Ratnavati, father Bhagavān and mother Dhammavati.

historical_events.event_name: Decoration of entrance door with brass plates
historical_events.event_description: In the memory of his deceased parents Wā Siṃha and Yaco, Vajrācārya Bikhvāraju had the entrance door clad with brass plates.

historical_events.event_name: Navadāna (Samyaka Mahādāna) was organized and consecrated caitya
historical_events.event_description: During the reign of King Surendra Bīr Vikram Śāha, Vajrācārya Bhikwāla, his wife Dhanalakṣmī and their son Bhīma Narasiṃha organised Navadāna (Samyaka Mahādāna) and consecrated the Caitya.
Dhanaju Śākya, his wife Pingalā and their daughter Bachalā consecrated the Śikharokūṭotpannajinālaya Caitya located at the northern side of the courtyard.

The bell hanging to the right side of thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥwas donated by Vajrācārya Harṣa Bahādur Siṃha, Vajrācārya Kula Bahādura Siṃha, Vajrācārya Ratna Raj, Vajrācārya Jīva Rāj, Vajrācāraya Pañca Bīr and other group members.

This Bāhāḥ was damaged due to the earthquake in 1934. The temple situated at the center of the Vihāra'scourtyard was also damaged. When the temple was renovated, its lower roof was removed. Now it is just a single-roofed temple.
